title: Infrastructure Alert: Unresponsive Node Taint Due to Low Memory
description: A monitoring alert has been triggered overnight indicating an unresponsive node due to low memory. The affected node is tainted and is currently unable to respond to requests.
resolution:
To resolve the issue, please follow these steps: 
1. Log in to the cluster control panel. 
2. Identify the affected node using its IP address or hostname. 
3. Check the memory usage of the node by running a command such as 'kubectl describe pod <pod-name>'. 
4. If memory usage is low, add more memory to the node. This can be done using a Kubernetes node tint configuration file. For example, you can create a file named 'node-tint.yaml' with the following content: 
```yaml
apiVersion: k8s.io/v1alpha3
xkind: NodeTintConfig
tools: 
  - memoryMaxLimit: <new-memory-limit>Mi
  - os: 
    kernel: <kernel-version>
```
5. Replace `<new-memory-limit>` with the desired maximum memory limit in MB and `<kernel-version>` with the version of your kernel. Save the file to the same directory as your kubeconfig file. 
6. Apply the node tint configuration using the command 'kubectl apply -f node-tint.yaml'. 
7. Verify that the memory usage has increased on the affected node by running the 'kubectl describe pod <pod-name>' command again. If the issue persists, please contact the system administrator for further assistance.

title: Infrastructure - Memory Exhaustion after Pod Restart
description: The application has been experiencing memory exhaustion after a pod restart. The average CPU usage and memory usage have been consistently high.
resolution:
The issue is likely caused by the use of cgroups. To resolve this, you can increase the limit on the memory used by the cgroup by editing the `/etc/cgroup-parent.conf` file. Here are the steps to do so: 
1. Open the `/etc/cgroup-parent.conf` file with a text editor
2. Add or modify the line corresponding to the cgroup for the application to increase the memory limit, e.g. `cpu.shares=0` or `memory.limit_in_bytes=1048576`. Replace the values as necessary for your application's needs 
3. Save and close the file
4. Restart the application's pod to apply the changes. After completing these steps, check the memory usage again and see if it has improved.
